analysis: Projected causal attention succeeded in this trial: host macro validation HR@10 reached 0.5375, versus the reported prior gated-attention result of 0.5188 (+0.0187 absolute). Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.5600, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.5500, Electronics 0.4800, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.5600. Electronics remains the weakest category. The result supports learned attention projections in this configuration, but one trial does not establish causality or robustness across seeds; prior per-category metrics were not supplied, so category-level improvements cannot be established. No held-out test results were available.
code_summary: One independently trained GRURec model per category uses 128-dimensional embeddings and a two-layer GRU, followed by jointly trained bias-free query, key, value, and context-output projections. Scaled causal attention masks padding safely; a sigmoid gate initialized with bias -2 adds context to recurrent features before LayerNorm, dropout, and output projection. Scores use tied item embeddings plus jointly trained item biases. Training retains sampled cross-entropy with 1,024 negatives, at most 2,048 target positions, and training-window negative masking. Validation selects one checkpoint per category by HR@10 with NDCG@10 tie-breaking. The predictor writer embeds the complete architecture, reconstructs each routed model from its saved configuration, and strictly loads its single selected checkpoint. No ensembles or independently fitted auxiliary scorers are used.
